records.issue_text: pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:45 — Unified create and update failures are recorded as legacy failures while legacy collection deletions are recorded as unified operations, corrupting backend error metrics.
records.rationale: The finding identifies real metric recording bugs in the diff. In Create() at line 45, when storage fails, it calls `d.recordLegacyDuration(true, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startStorage)` - recording a storage failure as a legacy duration. In DeleteCollection() at line 119, the goroutine calls `d.recordStorageDuration(err != nil, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startLegacy)` - recording legacy operation duration as storage duration. These are clear copy-paste errors that will corrupt the metrics by attributing errors and durations to the wrong backend.

records.issue_text: pkg/tests/apis/playlist/playlist_test.go:133 — Mode 3 tests immediately inspect legacy state even though legacy writes are asynchronous, making CRUD assertions race and flake.
records.rationale: The diff shows Mode 3 implementation uses goroutines for legacy writes (e.g., `go func() { ... d.Legacy.Create(...) }()` in dualwriter_mode3.go lines 44-51). The new Mode 3 tests in playlist_test.go (lines 129-143, 188-203, 283-310) call `doPlaylistTests` which likely performs CRUD operations and checks results. Since legacy writes are asynchronous in Mode 3, any test assertions that check legacy state immediately after operations could race. The finding correctly identifies that the test structure doesn't account for the async nature of Mode 3 legacy writes, which could cause flaky tests.
